results.title: Environmental, Social and Corporate Governance (ESG) and Total Factor Productivity: The Mediating Role of Financing Constraints and R&D Investment
results.content: # Environmental, Social and Corporate Governance (ESG) and Total Factor Productivity: The Mediating Role of Financing Constraints and R&D Investment. This study uses panel data analysis of 9125 observations from 1305 eligible companies to examine the relationship between ESG ratings, financing constraints, corporate research and development (R&D), and total factor productivity (TFP). ESG ratings; total factor productivity; financing constraints; firm research and development. While previous studies often focus on individual ESG components, this research integrates ESG performance as a holistic factor, highlighting how ESG practices enhance corporate productivity by easing financing constraints and boosting research and development (R&D) investments. This framework reveals that improved ESG performance enables companies to reduce financing constraints and increase R&D investment, indirectly fostering productivity growth—an area not fully explored in existing literature, especially within China’s highly polluting enterprises. : ESG ratings, research and development (R&D) and total factor productivity. Research and development (R&D) will serve as a mediating factor in the impact of ESG ratings on total factor productivity; higher ESG ratings are expected to increase research and development (R&D), thereby improving total factor productivity. It investigates the relationships among ESG ratings, financing constraints, corporate research and development (R&D), and total factor productivity (TFP) within this context. results.title: Digital transformation of energy enterprises, ESG performance, and green total factor productivity - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Digital transformation of energy enterprises, ESG performance, and green total factor productivity. Digital transformation has a significant promoting effect on the green total factor productivity of energy enterprises. Digital transformation boosts enterprise green productivity via ESG improvement. This paper takes A-share listed companies in China's energy industry from 2010 to 2023 as samples to systematically explore the internal correlation mechanism among digital transformation, ESG performance, and green total factor productivity (GTFP). The empirical results indicate that: digital transformation significantly enhances GTFP; digital transformation improves enterprise GTFP by enhancing corporate ESG performance; and the digital transformation performance elasticity of non-state-owned energy enterprises is significantly higher than that of state-owned enterprises. At present, Chinese enterprises are experiencing a swift digital transformation, with companies of all sizes—large, medium, and small—beginning to tightly integrate advanced technologies such as big data, blockchain, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing into their operational management. Therefore, investigating how digital reforms and ESG performance influence a company's green total factor productivity holds significant importance for fostering the high-quality development of companies and promoting sustainable economic and social progress. This paper takes the energy industry as the research object to deeply analyze the impact of digital transformation and explore the influencing pathways of ESG performance, providing certain reference value for the future digital transformation of energy enterprises. This paper conducts research from a previously unexplored perspective, positioning digital transformation in the power industry and studying the changes in corporate green total factor productivity brought about by digital transformation in the energy industry from an industry perspective. Digital transformation enables the intelligent interconnection and real-time data collection of energy production equipment through the introduction of technologies such as the Internet of Things and industrial internet. The maximum value of green total factor productivity (GTFP) for energy enterprises is 1.2123, the minimum value is 0.8079, and the mean value is 1.0138, indicating a certain degree of disparity in GTFP among enterprises. This paper conducts a comprehensive analysis of the interrelationships among digital transformation, ESG performance, and Green Total Factor Productivity (GTFP) in A-share listed energy companies from 2010 to 2023. ### Digital economy, human capital accumulation, and corporate green total factor productivity: based on strategic emerging industries.

results.title: How ESG governance affects total factor productivity: Evidence from Chinese listed companies - ScienceDirect
results.content: ESG governance increases total factor productivity by promoting green innovation and reducing operational risk. This study investigates the complex relationships among environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices and total factor productivity (TFP) in enterprises, which remains a topic of ongoing debate. In 2022, the report of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) proposed the goal of “accelerating the green transformation of the development mode” and “actively and steadily pushing forward carbon peaking and carbon neutrality.” These statements serve as guidelines for Chinese enterprises to engage in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices to improve the quality of their development, which is reflected mainly in the improvement of total factor productivity (TFP). Organizations such as the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) and the U.S. Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) have issued guidelines to standardize ESG disclosure and governance, enhancing corporate awareness of environmental impacts and social responsibilities. This highlights the increasing emphasis of companies on ESG governance as a critical means to mitigate environmental impacts, promote social justice, and combat climate change. The emphasis on environmentally friendly technologies under ESG governance encourages firms to adopt innovation-driven strategies (Liu et al., 2024). On the one hand, some studies have argued that ESG governance can enhance financial performance and firm value (Rahman et al., 2023), as ESG practices help strengthen corporate image and increase consumer and investor trust (Abdullah and Hashmi, 2024), thereby increasing revenue. On the basis of the above analysis, this paper selects 3970 A-share listed companies in China's Shanghai and Shenzhen markets between 2010 and 2023 as the research sample, aiming to explore the mechanism of the role of ESG governance in TFP improvement and its heterogeneous impacts. First, by constructing a dual-channel model that integrates green innovation and operational risk, this study pioneers the exploration of how ESG governance synergistically enhances TFP through two distinct yet complementary mechanisms, i.e., “technological innovation-driven efficiency gains” and “risk control-driven loss mitigation,” thereby advancing theoretical linkages between ESG governance and TFP. ### Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and financial outcomes: Analyzing the impact of ESG on financial performance. ### Unlocking environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance through energy efficiency and green tax: SEM-ANN approach.
